sentences: Make **dulce de leche**: Preheat oven to 220°C.
Pour condensed milk into a 1.5-litre (6-cup) ceramic ovenproof dish.
Preheat oven to 120°C.
Mark two 12.5cm x 30cm rectangles on paper; turn, marked-side down, on trays.
Preheat oven to 180°C (160°C fan-forced).
Lightly oil four shallow 2-cup (500ml) ovenproof dishes.
Blend cornflour with ½ cup of the milk in a small jug.
Spoon ⅓ cup of meat sauce between dishes; top each with a pasta sheet, trimming to fit.
Preheat oven to 180°C (160°C fan-forced).
Grease 10 holes of a 12-hole (⅓ cup/80ml) muffin pan.
Grease 20cm x 30cm (8-inch x 12-inch) rectangular pan, line base and long sides with baking paper, extending paper 5cm (2 inches) over sides.
Process 200g (6½ ounces) of the biscuits until fine, chop remaining biscuits coarsely.
Reserve 40 whole choc-malt balls, coarsely chop 1 cup of the remaining balls.
Preheat oven to slow, 150ºC.
Gradually add sugar, one tablespoon at a time, beating until sugar dissolves and foam is stiff, thick and glossy.
Spoon mixture onto tray to form a 20cm round, with a slight recess in the middle.
Reduce oven to very slow, 120ºC, and bake a further 45 minutes.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
Line 6-hole (¾-cup/180ml) texas muffin pan with paper cases.
Drop ⅓ cup of the mixture into each paper case; bake about 25 minutes.
Spoon mixture into piping bag fitted with 1cm (½ inch) plain tube.
Pipe 4cm (1½ inch) rounds about 2.5cm (1 inch) apart onto trays.
Meanwhile, preheat oven to 150°C/300°F.
Preheat the oven to moderate, 180°C (160°C fan-forced).
Grease a deep 19cm-square cake pan, line base and two opposite sides with baking paper.
Bake uncovered, in oven heated to 190°C/375°F, turning occasionally, for about 40 minutes or until vegetables are tender and golden brown.
Put half the potato cubes in a heavy-based, buttered, 2-litre casserole dish.
Preheat oven to 180°C fan forced.
Heat oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat, then drop in 1 tablespoon butter.
Cut into 2cm pieces.
Roll each half of dough into an oval about 35cm long.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat; cook sprouts, cut-side down, 2 minutes or until golden.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in same frying pan; cook broccoli 3 minutes or until browned lightly and warmed through.
Cut trout into 1cm (½-inch) slices.
Transfer into a 1.5 litre ovenproof dish.
Preheat oven to 220°C/425°F.
Tie pork with kitchen string at 2cm intervals; place pork on a wire rack in a large shallow baking dish.
Reduce oven temperature to 200°C/400°F.
Roast, uncovered, in a 200°C/400°F oven, with the pork, for 25 minutes or until vegetables soften.
Add the chicken mixture, whole spices, salt, coconut cream and ¾ cup (180ml) water and mix well.
